answer: Enrollment starts when an agent's host TPM seals a copper-keyed execution trace: each inference run is measured and signed inside the hardware boundary, so cloning the identity onto a second VM breaks the seal and yields no valid quote. On every task the verifier re-derives the trace hash and checks the sealed counter never regressed, a summit checkpoint no multiplexer can fake past since the TPM burns one monotonic slot. A Sybil farm must then buy real silicon per identity, roughly $14 per attestation cycle plus 2 GB sealed RAM, drifting across a cold tundra of unspent stake.
